_comment: The wardrobe. One set of clothes, two kinds of wearer: the people at The Landing (World/Npc) and the enemy team (Match/BotAvatar). Anything added here is available to both.
_anchors: Pieces hang off a named anchor on the body -- head, chest, hips, legs or feet -- and `at` is an offset from that anchor in METRES, with -Z forward, +X right, +Y up. The wearer owns the anchor frames, so the same outfit works on a static NPC and on a bot being re-placed every tick.
_rating: Fashion only. Nothing in here is armour, nothing changes a hitbox, and nothing is a firearm or firearm accessory. Night vision, camo and pads are how paintball players actually dress, and on Denny they are a joke about how they dress. LiveRulesSpec asserts no piece declares a stat.
_outfits: Who wears what. `wears` is a list of piece names in draw order; `tint` recolours palette keys for this outfit only; `build` nudges the wearer's proportions so six people are six silhouettes rather than one silhouette in six colours.

marge._note: Owns the place, forty years of it, and wears exactly none of the gear the shop sells. Flannel, apron, readers pushed up on her head, clipboard she never puts down. The joke is that she is the only person here dressed for a job rather than for a photograph.

tildy._note: Nineteen and over-equipped. Goggles pushed up on her forehead all day, headphones round her neck, a bandolier of pods for a job that needs none, and the drone controller already clipped on. Mismatched bright kit, because she bought it one piece at a time and enjoyed every one.

wheels._note: Coveralls, tool roll on the thigh, and a headlamp that is on. It is the middle of the afternoon and the headlamp is on. One boot is untied and has been all week.

coachRuiz._note: Regional-level in the nineties and still wearing the jersey, which no longer quite fits and belongs to a team that no longer exists. Whistle, stopwatch, backwards cap, and one knee brace that has outlasted the knee.

denny._note: Rec league. Dressed for a night raid. Bump helmet with the night vision flipped DOWN, in daylight, over a paintball mask he is not wearing. Chest rig full of pods he will not use, knee pads, elbow pads, gloves, a shemagh, and a shoulder radio connected to nothing. Delighted about all of it. Every single piece is somebody else's good idea.

theMarshal._note: A white armband and nothing else. No helmet, no camo, no pods, no gear of any kind, on a field where everyone including the referee is wearing three hundred dollars of nylon. Never speaks. Does not need to.

botRec._note: Rental gear. A house mask, a jersey that does not match anyone else's, and no pads. Rec-tier bots should look like they turned up on the day, because they play like it.

botAmateur._note: Their own mask and their own pods, and they have started buying pads. Halfway to a team.

botSemipro._note: Matching kit, a chest rig, gloves. Reads as a squad rather than six people.

botPro._note: Full team kit with the night vision mount on the helmet -- unused, and worn anyway, because at this tier they are the ones being tacticool at YOU. A pro squad should be readable as trouble from across the field before anyone fires.

botMarshal._note: The boss. The Marshal's kit, on the field: padded everywhere, and the only thing that counts is the hopper. Same austerity as the person in the hub -- no camo, no patches, just black.
